item.title: Sheikh Hamdan approves Dubai Longevity Authority's strategy and budget
item.description: Sheikh Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum, Crown Prince of Dubai, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence of the UAE, and Chairman of The Executive Council of Dubai, approved the strategy and operating budget of the Dubai Longevity Authority (DLA) following the inaugural board meeting of the Authority, which operates under Hamdan’s Presidency.The approvals represent the next phase in the Dubai Longevity Authority's development, moving it from establishment to implementation as the world's first dedicated regulator for the Longevity, Wellness and Advanced Health (LWAH) sector, advancing a sector defined not by how long people live, but by how long they live in good health.Sheikh

item.title: Total economic value of GCC tourism reaches $254.7 billion
item.description: The report on Strategic Tourism Ambition in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) Countries, issued by the GCC Statistical Centre (GCC-Stat), indicated that the direct and indirect economic value of tourism in the GCC countries rose to approximately $254.7 billion in 2025, compared with $11.7 trillion globally.The number of tourism-related jobs in the GCC countries reached approximately 4.5 million, compared with around 371 million globally, while tourism’s contribution to gross domestic product (GDP) and employment, as well as the sector’s growth rates in the GCC, stood at competitive levels compared with global averages.The report, which examines the sector’s ability to withstand ge

item.title: Google plans first test of AI chips in space under Project Suncatcher
item.description: Google plans to launch the first test of its Project Suncatcher orbital data centre on 1st October to assess how its Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) AI chips perform in the harsh conditions of space.The mission will evaluate how the chips handle radiation, vibration and the physical stresses of launch, while also testing cooling systems, one of the biggest challenges of operating computing hardware in space.Google's cooling system uses heat pipes to transfer heat from the chips to radiators that dissipate it into space. item.title: China's tech giant Alibaba to expand data centre footprint in UAE among other nations over next 12 months
item.description: Chinese tech giant Alibaba unveiled plans on Wednesday to expand its overseas data centres, targeting markets across Europe and the Middle East. The company said it would "establish its first cloud regions" in Turkey, Finland and the Netherlands, while "expanding its data centre footprint in Malaysia, Germany, the United Arab Emirates, France and Hong Kong" over the next 12 months. Hangzhou-based Alibaba is one of the frontrunners in China's artificial intelligence industry, with its Qwen model among the world's most downloaded AI models. item.title: Women in Technology 2026 places women at heart of future of AI and tech
